title: Sukuma Lake Fish Soup
localName: Supu ya Samaki wa Ziwa — Wasukuma
community: Sukuma people of Lake Victoria — the lakeside fish soup tradition
author: Mama Salima
desc: Sukuma Lake Fish Soup — whole tilapia or Nile perch simmered with tomatoes, onions, and local herbs in the minimal-spice Sukuma tradition. The lakeside soup of Tanzania's largest ethnic group — the freshest possible fish from Lake Victoria, simply prepared.
longDesc: Sukuma fish soup is the dish that has fed the people around Lake Victoria for millennia — the fresh fish of the lake prepared with minimal intervention to let the quality speak. The Sukuma traditionally added very few spices, relying instead on the extraordinary freshness of the lake fish.
ingredients: 800g whole tilapia or Nile perch — cleaned and gutted
steps: Combine fish, onion, garlic, and water in a pot.
Bring to a boil. Skim foam.
Remove fish. Flake gently. Return to broth.
Season. Garnish with coriander. Serve with lemon.
chefTips: The freshness of Lake Victoria tilapia needs no elaborate spicing.
Lemon at the table is essential — the Sukuma squeeze generously.
cookingScience: See TZA080 for fish soup science.
sustainabilityTips: Lake Victoria tilapia supports millions of Sukuma fishing families — buying locally caught fish from them directly is the most sustainable choice.
culturalNote: Sukuma lake fish soup is the taste of Lake Victoria — the great freshwater sea that defines the geography, economy, and culture of Tanzania's most populous people. To eat this soup is to understand why the Sukuma have always lived by the lake.
